notes.byline: Results from October 5 and 6, 2026. Public LAVA evidence; focused follow-up to the October 4 integration run.
notes.index_summary: SystemReady fixes, UNO Q CPU_ON fix, synchronous NPU latency and remoteproc restart validation
notes.footer: Arm suite verdicts and LAVA case counts are different measures. No overall Arm compliance is claimed. Download this report data.

inf1.method: INF-1 follow-up, 2026-10-05: two original/updated pairs on the same boot per board, using the current integration images. Only the HTP command adds --synchronous. QNN CPU and TensorFlow Lite CPU/GPU commands are unchanged. MobileNetV2, seven images, five warm-ups and 51 measured inferences per run. Bars average the two run means; whiskers average the per-run p50 and p90, not pooled percentiles. Original VENTUNO Q NPU values include async queue wait. Updated NPU values are synchronous per-inference NETRUN times including host/runtime overhead, not accelerator-only times or throughput.
inf1.ordering: NPU ordering, fastest first: original test, RB3 Gen 2 < Lemans EVK (IQ-9075) < VENTUNO Q; synchronous test, VENTUNO Q < RB3 Gen 2 < Lemans EVK (IQ-9075). The change corrects the latency measurement; these jobs reuse the same firmware, kernel, runtimes and model.
inf1.limitations: These are two repeats on one boot per board, not a survey of device or boot variability. CPU/GPU timings differ despite unchanged commands; these pairs do not isolate clock, thermal or preceding-workload effects. The first VENTUNO Q attempt (471041) hit the existing F20 GPU boot failure: HFI_H2F_MSG_PREPARE_SLUMBER timed out and the first original-test GPU correctness checks failed. It remains in the evidence; the VENTUNO Q table uses the complete repeat with passing correctness checks. No image was rebuilt. Test-definitions commit a5c05a15 is local and has not been published.

rb3g2.note: Job 471042: original 33802ad7 and updated a5c05a15, alternated twice on one boot. The original backend already falls back to synchronous execution; the explicit option keeps the same latency semantics.

sections.title: 1. What changed
sections.html:
The October 2 SystemReady fixes are now folded into the integration stack: VENTUNO Q SCT is Compliant, UNO Q SCT has one remaining failure, and RB3 Gen 2 completes ACS. Lemans still encounters F16. The subsequent UNO Q investigation identifies and fixes the older CPU_ON defect; all BSA PE cases pass, with five timer/wake failures still open.

New in this dated entry: the folded SystemReady runs, standard-plan comparisons, UNO Q root cause and final validation, and LPASS/PAS TEE restart evidence. Carried: the October 4 integration baselines, existing open findings, and the October 5 INF-1 paired measurements already prepared in the prior local render. INF-1 is repeated here with the same values, not a new firmware speedup or another test run.

These are separate experiments on their recorded images, not a single combined image containing every fix. The October 4 report retains its full case inventory, components and older findings.

UNO Q interpretation updated: the folded run has nine BSA PE failures after CPU 2 stops completing CPU_ON. The later crossover tests show the defect already exists in the baseline and is device-sensitive. The original before/after comparison changed devices as well as software. The CPU_ON fix restores the PE cases; it is a separate follow-up, not a rewrite of the Arm verdict recorded for 471088.

UNO Q retains one SCT failure for unsupported EFI network capability. Its two changed boot-partition read failures, and the four Lemans read failures, match the prior rescan race (SystemReady F15), but missing individual read errors limit that attribution to an inference. VENTUNO Q BSA stays at four failures because B_PPI_00 is repaired while B_TIME_09 becomes a failure. RB3 B_TIME_09 is skipped at the documented standby limit. 471088, 471093, 471094, 471091

Open: Lemans F16 still aborts twice. The first fault reaches SCT data; the cause of the control-flow error is unisolated, and the second fault does not establish the same mechanism. All 27 LAVA power-cycle interventions are test recovery, not successful firmware resets; final Linux shutdown also times out. 471093 The rare VENTUNO Q XBL hang after media_init:2 remains open: absence in the folded run is not proof of a fix, and the SAIL timeout also occurs on successful boots. 469812, 470192, 471094

Carried workarounds: random MAC fallbacks on VENTUNO Q and Lemans retain the tested Ethernet behavior. They do not establish persistent VENTUNO Q addressing or repair Lemans EEPROM/QUP probe ordering. No F16 fix or rare-XBL-hang fix is established by this change set.

sections.title: 4. UNO Q CPU_ON hotplug fix
sections.html:
Fixed locally Agatti CPU_OFF leaves the core powered in WFI. The old CPU_ON path nevertheless repeats the cold power-up sequence, changing memory-power and retention controls on a core whose supply never collapsed. The fix detects an already-powered core, preserves those controls and pulses only core reset. First cold power-up is unchanged. The exact internal stall instruction, individual offending power bit and electrical reason for device susceptibility remain unobserved.

Crossover tests show baseline and SR both fail on Device A and both pass on Device B. A rebuilt unmodified image, a data-layout-only control and a read-only control still fail on Device A; the uninstrumented reset change passes. Tracing masks the failure and is not the fix. 471177, 471176, 471179, 471180, 471185, 471193, 471216, 471190

This is BSA-only validation, not a new full ACS verdict. 471207

sections.title: 6. Remoteproc restart fixes
sections.html:
LPASS AG NoC sideband flag

New A/B evidence The Lemans OP-TEE change clears the AG NoC sideband manager port 1 output flag after releasing the LPASS halt request. Both the baseline 471002 and patched 471003 pass the restart matrix. Each DSP has three stop/start cycles: 18 step checks plus a presence check. These are 19 test cases per DSP, not 19 restart cycles.

DSPBaseline 471002Patched 471003
ADSP19 / 19 pass19 / 19 pass
CDSP19 / 19 pass19 / 19 pass
CDSP119 / 19 pass19 / 19 pass
GPDSP019 / 19 pass19 / 19 pass
GPDSP119 / 19 pass19 / 19 pass

Both jobs pass all seven runtime fingerprint checks and poweroff. Both retain the deliberate missing-device negative and kernel warning/call-trace failures. The patched job also fails CDSP/CDSP1 boot smoke checks, matching the existing F15 boot-crash finding; measured restart cases still pass. A/B validates the added reset writes without showing a restart improvement, since the baseline also passes. The build-only report predates these runtime results.

PAS TEE NULL resource table

Fixed in the Linux TEE backend Stopping a remote processor clears the cached table pointer but can leave a nonzero size. If restart has no input resource table, the TEE backend uses that stale size and copies from NULL. The fix normalizes NULL input to zero size before both the TEE size query and the copy. Real input tables remain unchanged; the generic remoteproc caller is unchanged.

The failing control 467335 faults at qcom_pas_tee_get_rsc_table() on first restart. The earlier caller-fix reference 467339 passes the restart matrix. The new backend-fix jobs below test the replacement fix; a regression harness also reproduces the original fault and passes all 15 fixed cases, including failure paths.

sections.title: 7. Unusual findings, flagged for investigation
sections.html: Status is scoped to the cited experiment. Finding IDs come from their respective test reports; SystemReady and standard-plan numbering are not interchangeable. The earlier flagged findings and known-issue inventory remain carried unless explicitly updated here; this follow-up does not rerun all historical maxcpus, negative-control or boot-timing experiments.

findings.title: UNO Q CPU_ON: cause identified and fixed
findings.text: New evidence supersedes the earlier SR-only attribution. The defect predates the SR fold and is device-sensitive. The powered-core reset change restores hotplug and all BSA PE cases; the complete BSA suite still has five failures.

findings.title: UNO Q timer/wake failures remain open
findings.text: Carried timer/wake findings remain after the CPU fix: B_TIME_07, B_TIME_08, B_TIME_09, B_WAK_03 and B_WAK_07. Neither BSA compliance nor full SystemReady compliance follows from the PE fix.

findings.title: Lemans SCT aborts and reset recovery remain open
findings.text: New folded run reproduces both SCT aborts. No established F16 fix is present. Power-cycle recovery does not turn failed reset or SCT cases into passes; final Linux shutdown also times out.

findings.title: Rare VENTUNO Q XBL reset hang remains open
findings.text: Carried hang after media_init:2; not reproduced in the folded run. The SAIL timeout alone is not diagnostic because successful boots print it too. No isolated cause or established fix.

findings.title: VENTUNO Q display and GPU correctness failures recur
findings.text: New standard runs reproduce the known display vblank warning and the GMU timeout with incorrect GPU results on separate boots. Both failures are retained. Passing latency checks do not establish correct inference.

findings.title: Lemans unsigned-PD and warm-reset failures recur
findings.text: Both new standard runs reproduce the unsigned-PD session errors and absent warm-boot banners. These are changed failures against the named baselines where applicable, not clean standard-plan passes.

findings.title: RB3 frequency readback passes once; PMU variation remains
findings.text: New observation updates the earlier description of an always-failing minimum-frequency check. This one passing result establishes no fix; PMU failures remain within the baseline pair.

findings.title: INF-1 measures synchronous per-inference latency
findings.text: Carried October 5 measurement correction: VENTUNO Q changes from 7.812 ms including async queue wait to 0.403 ms synchronous NETRUN time. Firmware and CPU/GPU commands are unchanged. UNO Q has no NPU and its QNN CPU backend remains unsupported by QAIRT.

findings.title: LPASS A/B passes restart cases; boot faults remain
findings.text: Both sides pass all restart cases, so no measured restart improvement is claimed. The patched boot has additional CDSP/CDSP1 smoke failures. Both retain kernel warning/trace failures and the expected negative.

findings.title: PAS fix validated with a failed FastRPC run retained
findings.text: The backend NULL-copy fix passes VENTUNO Q and the Lemans repeat. The first Lemans matrix fails a kernel-clean check during a concurrent FastRPC release oops. Its exact race was not re-diagnosed; boot smoke and idle warnings remain separate carried findings.
